column1: DayBreak — Social Media Problem & Solution Research

The strongest research does not support treating all social-media use as equally harmful. DayBreak should redesign the specific mechanisms that create harm—including engagement optimization, social comparison, harmful amplification, weak privacy, opaque ranking, and moderation failures—while preserving connection, identity exploration, creativity, learning, and community support.
1. Optimize for session value, not session length
column2: Ask whether a session helped the user connect, learn, create, or recover—not merely whether the user stayed on the platform.

column1: 2. Give users control over ranking goals
column2: Allow users to choose ranking modes such as Calm, Connect, Learn, Explore, or Chronological. Explain why recommendations appear.
Keep useful analytics private while reducing public like counts, streak pressure, follower-based status, and other popularity signals.

column1: 4. Use targeted friction at high-risk moments
column2: Add pauses, context, and circuit breakers before resharing misinformation, joining pile-ons, continuing late-night sessions, or repeatedly viewing sensitive content.

column1: 5. Make youth privacy and safety the default
column2: Minimize data collection, restrict unsafe adult-to-minor contact, avoid behavioral advertising to minors, and include young people in product design.

column1: 6. Measure wellbeing and meaningful connection directly
column2: Track autonomy, sleep disruption, harmful exposure, meaningful interaction, satisfaction, and session value—not only engagement or time spent.
